questions.text: Explain the functions of the United Nations Security Council.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the functions of the United Nations Security Council. (Difficult)

answer.value: The Security Council is the executive organ of the United Nations. Its primary functions are to maintain international peace and security and to make recommendations on matters considered by the General Assembly. It consists of 15 member states. Of these, the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, France, and China are permanent members, while the other ten members are elected by the General Assembly for a two-year term. For a resolution to be adopted, it requires the approval of at least nine members. However, if any one of the five permanent members votes against it (exercises the veto), the resolution cannot be adopted.

questions.text: Mention any two limitations of the United Nations.
questions.text_as_printed: Mention any two limitations of the United Nations. (Difficult)

answer.value: After the disintegration of the Soviet Union and the end of the Cold War, the United States emerged as the dominant global power, creating challenges for a balanced, multipolar world order. The United Nations has been unable to implement many of its resolutions effectively because it does not have its own standing army and depends on the military support of its member states. When member states refuse to provide military assistance, the UN faces difficulties in resolving conflicts.
